Q: How can I call other subcommands?
body:
I have built an cli application like this:
```bash
$ app apply sth1
$ app apply sth2
...
$ app apply sthn
```
Now, I want to add another subcommand `all`, like this
```bash
$ app apply all
```
This command will execute all the logic of sth1, sth2, ...., sthn.

Naturally, I don't want to duplicate codes,  so I have two options:

* use `cmd.Run`
```golang
allCmd := &cobra.Command{
  User: "all",
  Run: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) {
    sth1Cmd.Run(cmd, args)
    sth2Cmd.Run(cmd, args)
    // ....
    sthnCmd.Run(cmd, args)
  }
}
```
This option has some cons. If other command has defined `PreRun` or `PostRun`, it will ignore those code. And those flags defined on those command will be ignored, too.

* use `Execute`
```golang
allCmd := &cobra.Command{
  User: "all",
  Run: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) {
    sth1Cmd.Execute()
    sth2Cmd.Execute()
    // ....
    sthnCmd.Execute()
  }
}
```
This option is just not work. Because `Execute` will find every command's root command to execute. And all subcommands have same parent command, it will cause stackoverflow.

Can anybody give me some advices? Thank you!

Q: Does cobra support "@file.txt" flag syntax?
body:
On Windows there's limit of 32k bytes per single CLI command, which makes running of longer commands impossible.
To overcome, some tools like gcc/clang/msvc use what I call "@file.txt syntax". 
It's when all flags are saved in a text file, one per line, and then consumed by the compiler like this:

```bash
gcc -Iinclude -Wall example.c      #1

# becomes
echo "-Iinclude\n-Wall\nexample.c" > flags.txt
gcc @flags.txt # functionally same as #1
```
With this syntax we can run CLI commands of arbitrary lengths on Windows.

Does cobra support this syntax?

P.S. example with python's argparse: https://docs.python.org/3/library/argparse.html#fromfile-prefix-chars

Q: How to do auto-completions for Cobra CLIs that are `os.Exec`ed
body:
Say I have `program-A` which has auto-completions turned on. `program-A` performs an `os.Exec` on a subsequent Cobra CLI `program-B` and is effectively a thin wrapper around `program-B`. `program-B` also has auto-completions.

So, an execution might look like:
```
$ program-A run --path /some/path --config /some/config
```

Which under the hood is really just running:
```
$ program-B run --path /some/path --config /some/config
```

Where `--path /some/path --config /some/config` is essentially being forwarded on as a string.

I have `run` defined as a command in `program-A` and it shows auto-completions for that command, but since I'm `os.Exec`ing the rest of the command / flags, it'd be nice to find a way to have auto-completions bubble up through `program-B` to `program-A`

---

Is there any way to do this? Maybe @marckhouzam knows or has some good ideas?

Q: Is it possible to easily hide default flag values from help?
body:
I have a command that displays the following in its help text:
```
Flags:
  -h, --help            help for sample
  -e, --enable-screen   Turn the screen on (default false)
  -S, --no-sound        Turn the sound off (default true)
  -s, --seed uint       Supply a randomization seed (default 9309262286194859912)
```
The default value for `seed` is supplied as `rand.Uint64()` so it is randomly generated every time the help is printed and will not be the actual value used when the flag is not supplied. Because of this, I would like to stop that flag from printing the default value into the help text.

I could do this by using 0 as a sentinel value, by adding a layer of indirection with a second variable, or by overriding the help text template, but all these approaches are rather inconvenient when the text itself is the only thing I'd like to change.

Similarly, I find the `(default true)` for the `--no-sound` option not entirely intuitive. I can, of course, explain it one way or the other in the description, or change the option name itself to make it less ambiguous, but again I'd prefer not to have to change the behavior or interface of my app just to make the help text easier to understand.

I'm very new to Cobra, but didn't see any clear way to disable the display of default values either on a per-flag basis or globally. Is there a way to do this without resorting to the approaches mentioned above?

Q: How to test inherited flags?
body:

```go

                err := cmd.Execute()
                assert.Error(t, err)
        })
        t.Run("no repo with -R", func(t *testing.T) {
                cmd.SetArgs([]string{"-R", "forkrepo"})
                err := cmd.Execute()
                assert.NoError(t, err)
        })
```

The problem is that `-R` is defined in parent command, so the test fails.

```go
cmd.InheritedFlags().StringP("repo", "R", "", "Select another repository.")
```

So how to test that?
